utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Madam Registrar, call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. This is the case number, IT-99-36-T, the Prosecutor versus Radoslav Brdjanin and Momir Talic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Brdjanin, good afternoon to you. Can you hear me in a language that you can understand? THE ACCUSED BRDJANIN: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honour. I can hear you and understand you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you. General Talic, good afternoon to you. Can you hear me in a language that you can understand? THE ACCUSED TALIC: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honour. I can hear you in a language I understand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. THE ACCUSED TALIC: [Interpretation] But the mike isn't working.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Please check -- yes, it's working now, your microphone. It's working now. Okay. You may sit down, General Talic. Thank you. Appearances for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Joanna Korner and Anna Richterova assisted by Denise Gustin case manager, good afternoon, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Good afternoon to you, Ms. Korner. Appearances for Radoslav Brdjanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRBOJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honours. My name is Trbojevic. With me is lead counsel, Mr. Ackerman, and our assistant Marela Jevtovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, and good afternoon to you. Appearances for General Talic.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Mr. President, Your Honours. I am Natasha Ivanovic-Fauveau, representing General Talic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you. Good afternoon to you. I understand there are some preliminaries? Yes, Madam Fauveau.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] First of all, I should like to draw attention to a problem of interpretation. Yesterday on page 71 of the LiveNote, I said I was not discussing the conditions at the hospital. This was translated as: [In English] "I don't contest the conditions that may have prevailed in that hospital." [Interpretation] Actually I don't think that that is the fault of the interpreters, because the word "debattre" has several meanings in the French language. But what I wanted to say was at this point in time I was not debating -- I was not addressing myself to the conditions in the hospital. Another point is that I should like to ask the permission of the Chamber to be able in the presence of the registrar or someone -- some other official, if I may examine the Red Cross documents in the possession of the witness, because I have serious doubts to -- serious doubts as to the fact that the witness does not have two documents but in fact three documents in his possession.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Well, if he has three and he has chosen to bring forward two, I'm not going to let you have the third one unless you tell me -- you give me a good reason. But it's -- if -- he has no right -- he is under no obligation -- he was under no obligation to bring those two documents in the first place.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, what he says is that these documents show that he was in the prison in Tunjice, and I am contesting that. And I think that those documents don't prove it. They put -- he put two documents together to prove that. And these are separate documents. And if we look at them separately, there's absolutely no proof.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It seems to me that he had two documents yesterday. We'll call him. If he still has them -- there's no question of not having a photocopy of the same documents, because they were handed over to the usher, and the usher went to photocopy straight away. So unless it's a question of authenticity, I don't even see why you should even look at the originals again. But if he has them and it is necessary to see them again, we'll see them again. But otherwise, the -- I have no reason, and I see no plausible reason, why the -- what you have, what you were given yesterday, whether that is in reality the document that he showed us yesterday. And that's about it. I mean, I'm not going to force a witness to show us other documents that he doesn't want to show us -- if he has them.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The document that is he showed us are three documents and not two.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We'll check that. I only saw two. I am not excluding that he may have a third -- may have had a third one yesterday, but I only saw two.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If you look at the photocopy of DT18 Defence exhibit, it is quite clear that these are two separate documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Oh, yes, that I remember. That, I remember. Because this document had this small piece of paper in front -- folding and lifting it. So this -- if you want to consider it as a separate piece of paper, yes, it is a separate piece of paper. But it was attached to this one. And then the other document that he had was this one. They were photocopied by the usher, so it's -- there's no question of not having photocopied the document that is the witness had. I don't understand you -- I don't understand the logic behind your -- your request at this point.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My only problem is the problem --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We'll get the documents.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- DT18. Because there's absolutely no proof that the document at the bottom is attached to the document on top. And it doesn't -- the document that mentions the prison of Tunjice does not bear the name of the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Bring the witness --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... we're just searching the transcript. The witness is actually saying -- and it may be that better be clarified -- he was in Banja Luka Hospital in a ward that had been assigned to people from --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: The urology and then -- the urology ward there was a cell. That's what he kept saying yesterday.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: First 8 and then 9.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. But it's Banja Luka Hospital. It's not the actual prison itself. Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That's for sure. We're not talking of a prison compound outside -- outside the hospital of Banja Luka. Definitely not.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. That was quite clear during the testimony of the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So the witness. Now, we have a problem. You're not the only ones with problems. Fortunately I -- due to an emergency I need to leave today and not later than 6.00. So in other words, we need to finish a little bit earlier. May I rely on your cooperation and have one break only, instead of two today? Yes. But first we'll go step by step.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have no problem with that. And let me just say while I'm on my feet that I had difficulty with scheduling next week, and I'm actually arriving back in The Hague on Monday. My flight is due to arrive at Schiphol at around 11.00. It shouldn't cause my problem with my being here at 2.15. But I just want to alert you to the problem that if there's a weather problem or something like that, I'm running on a pretty tight window there. But there's not much I can do about it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. That will be understandable. And in any case, I can guarantee you that the Tribunal will take all the necessary measures --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, it is in fact -- unfortunately the whole business is now creating a problem, because we slowed up. Unlike everybody else, I'm going to have the deal with the Stakic case next week, and I'm going to be in court calling a witness next week and Stakic is not sitting on Friday. And it's a long witness, Thursday and -- Wednesday and Thursday of next week. This witness we're about to call next is clearly not going to finish today in chief. So it may be that on the Monday week I'm going to find myself in two courts at the same time with a witness. And how we're going to resolve that is something I'm quite unclear about.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Madam Korner, when these problems arise, just make a suggestion and we'll come along. Because as long as these things don't happen capriciously, you will find the full understanding of the Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So, tell me what you would like and I will accommodate you has I will accommodate the Defence if these problems arise.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, what I'm hoping to do is to complete the witness in the Stakic case in chief in the two days -- we're sitting all day, I understand, in the Stakic case next week. And then have somebody else take over at that stage, because it's more difficult to have another lawyer take over a witness in mid-stream. But I'm just raising that in case it arises. But can I just tell Your Honours that we've reorganised the witness list.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, I see that.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Because again we have to get in the witnesses. 7.139 and 143 are the witnesses who are both reluctant to attend and had to be persuaded. And we gave them a date. So they need to come in definitely next week, as does the next witness, 7.52. So we -- I'm afraid we've had to alter the order again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So -- so number 27 --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Number 27 will follow on, I should imagine at the moment it's now going to be Tuesday. And then number 28, 29, and 30. They are all what I call effectively crime base witnesses.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mm-hm.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: So I would hope that we could get through them fairly quickly. And then 7.52 will be testifying here on Friday. And then the following week in the Stakic case. So again, I'd hope that we could complete his evidence in total on the Friday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Please try to liaise as much as you can with the Defence so that this is pretty much clear for -- it would be pretty much clear for them as well to know exactly what to expect and when, because it's more important for the Defence than it is for the -- for the Trial Chamber because we most of the time listen while they have to prepare --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, that's why this list has been prepared.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yeah. But in other words, is this what you provided today the correct -- the final? Or are you even -- are you changing this too?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: This is the final.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: That's a change from the list that we last gave you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Oh, yes. That's definite. That definitely is a change.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So we start with 7.13?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: No. On Monday, whatever it is, the 17th or whatever, it will be still the witness from today I anticipate.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yeah. Okay. All right. And after this will come --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: After that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: 7.13 will be immediately after.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes. And Your Honour, we're considerably trying to reduce the list as well and we'll reduce this list even more.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. That will be even before. You see, without imposing you get the same result sometimes even better. Without imposing.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Oh, I'm sorry. I see what Your Honour -- sorry. I'd lost Your Honour for a moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: This is why I try to make you all understand that -- why I stick to the system that I have adopted, because more or less it gives you the opportunity to take decisions better. And that way we move ahead. Good. Anyway, where is the witness?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Stojic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Would you kindly repeat once more today the solemn declaration that you made yesterday.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you. By any chance -- yesterday you showed us some documents that you had from the Red Cross. Do you have them here with you today?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Can I have a look at them, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: What's this other document in the back here? What is it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My brothers, Ivo and Ante, sent me a visa for entry into the Republic of Croatia.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Do you want to see that?

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Usher, please show these documents to Madam Fauveau and then to the Prosecutor and to Mr. Ackerman, for whatever they are worth. Are you interested in that other document that we didn't see yesterday?

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President. But I think it would perhaps be better for me to begin with my cross-examination and things will be clarified through the cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Do you have any objection at all that we photocopy that document too?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So we'll have it photocopied once Mr. Ackerman and Madam -- and Ms. Korner have finished with it.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I have here a visa too with the stamp indicating when I crossed the border into the Republic of Croatia.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And it was given to me in Caritas.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like it to be copied, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. So we'll photocopy that too and we'll have it distributed. And in the meantime, you can hand this document to Ms. Korner -- to Madam Fauveau, and it will take its round, if it is important.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The next document I have is from the municipal Red Cross organisation of Banja Luka, which I used as a pass to reach Novska -- it served as a pass for me to reach Novska.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Are you interested in that as well, Madam Fauveau?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'd like this to be disclosed too.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can't comment when I don't know what the document says.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: No. But he told you what it is. Anyway, we'll photocopy that too and then we'll decide whether you want to have them admitted as -- He has a lot of documents here, and I don't want to go ahead having to go through each and every one of these documents. I mean, it doesn't make sense. Madam Fauveau, please, your cross-examination. Yes. Photocopy them and then we'll see them later.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the registrar give the witness DT19, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This document was issued in Zagreb, the 27th of January 1993?

utterances.speaker: GRGO STOJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: It is a form of the Red Cross, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: GRGO STOJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: And on this form, certain information was written in advance, whereas other information is added case by case, on a case-by-case basis, regarding the person in question; is that right?

utterances.speaker: GRGO STOJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What do you mean a case-by-case basis?

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: For instance, if you look at the fourth line, it says "in prison." Those are the words to be found on the printed form.

utterances.speaker: GRGO STOJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: Whereas "Banja Luka" was added subsequently.

utterances.speaker: GRGO STOJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You have to add. It is a form that needs to be filled in.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: And on this form, after the word "Banja Luka," there is no "Tunjice," -- the word "Tunjice," does not appear.

utterances.speaker: GRGO STOJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But you have it on another document where it says "Tunjice."

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: My question is with respect to this document. I'm asking you about this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Madam Fauveau, why -- I cannot allow a witness to justify the entries in a document for which he is not responsible. I mean, these entries were made by other persons. Unless you are suggesting that he made those entries.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: How can you expect him to give you an explanation?

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You should ask from the person -- what persons who are responsible for the entries in these documents.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't think that a representative of the Red Cross will come to testify here. This document was issued in Croatia in 1993.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And do you expect him to answer you, to explain to you --

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... and in another one there isn't?

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'll come to the other document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Then come to the other document.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I should like no know whether the witness knows regarding document DT19. It is indicated that the document was done on the basis of a statement by the authorities.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know whether those authorities were Croatian authorities?

utterances.speaker: GRGO STOJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That refers to the authorities in Banja Luka.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: But that is not indicated on the document.

utterances.speaker: GRGO STOJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is indicated on another document.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: But on this one it is not indicated.

utterances.speaker: GRGO STOJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What is your aim? Are you contesting the accuracy of the International Committee of the Red Cross?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Stojic, please don't argue with the lawyer, with Defence counsel, who is here to do her duty. So don't argue with her. Answer the question. If it is not a legitimate question, I will stop you from answering, but otherwise just answer the question. No arguments, please. And I'm sure you understand. Yes, Madam Fauveau.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that on this document which authorities are in question is not indicated?

utterances.speaker: GRGO STOJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have no comment to make to such questions.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the registrar give the witness document DT18, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: There are indeed two documents on this piece of paper; isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: GRGO STOJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is true.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: The first is a message which Ante and Ivo Stojic sent you while you were still at the hospital in Banja Luka; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: GRGO STOJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: And the visa was attached to that document; is that true?

utterances.speaker: GRGO STOJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: So actually you received this document while you were at the hospital in Banja Luka together with the visa.

utterances.speaker: GRGO STOJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not receive that document in Banja Luka at all. It is clearly stated up there next to the stamp that the Croatian Red Cross took over from the International Committee of the Red Cross on the 25th of February, 1993. And I was already in Croatia then.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: I see well that that is what it says on top and also on the bottom it says "11th of December, Tunjice, released." The problem is that nothing proves that this was entered by the Red Cross. Nothing on this document prove that is?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Well, that's an argument. That's a submission, Madam Fauveau, not a question. So don't answer that question.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: To enter Croatia, you needed a visa, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: GRGO STOJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: And before entering Croatia, you didn't receive the visa.

utterances.speaker: GRGO STOJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: How did you obtain it?

utterances.speaker: GRGO STOJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I obtained it in Caritas in Banja Luka.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: And how did Caritas obtain the visa, if you know?

utterances.speaker: GRGO STOJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You need to ask a representative of Caritas that.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: So according to you, the Croatian authorities at the same time issued two visas for one and the same person.

utterances.speaker: GRGO STOJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The visa was copied and certified as being authentic.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. The two visas that you showed here have been certified. I agree with you fully. The document at the very bottom of DT18 actually is a photocopy. You don't have the original of that document?

utterances.speaker: GRGO STOJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's a photocopy, yes. But on the back, it has been certified. So it is a trustworthy document. I have the original on me.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: In any event, that document makes no mention of your name.

utterances.speaker: GRGO STOJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Which one?

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: The small piece of paper at the very bottom where a person was liberated on the 11th of December, 1992 from the Tunjice prison.

utterances.speaker: GRGO STOJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, it is attached to the message of the International Committee of the Red Cross.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: And this Red Cross message is where?

utterances.speaker: GRGO STOJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In Banja Luka.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: So the Red Cross in Banja Luka gave you only this piece of paper without your name, without your address, without anything.

utterances.speaker: GRGO STOJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My name is indicated here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Madam Richterova.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: I have an objection, because I can't see any point of this cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It's not completely relevant. But my objection would be that the witness has already answered this question. He said one was attached to the other. That's how he got it.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This document is a message from family members of the witness to the witness, through the intermediary of the Red Cross. It is not a message from the Red Cross of Banja Luka to the witness. So my question is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... an argument. Put a question, and we move. Because this is becoming impossible.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: Did you receive any other message from the Red Cross together with the small document at the bottom of Exhibit DT19. [In English] DT18.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Sorry. DT18.

utterances.speaker: GRGO STOJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was all that was attached to that message. And a second message - just a moment, please - is this one that I received from my brother. That is the one I received while in prison in the hospital. It was given -- brought to me by a delegate of the International Committee of the Red Cross.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I mean, it's two, three sheets of paper. And frankly I don't know the relevance of them, why they are here in the first place. I admitted the first two yesterday.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Well, I think we're entitled to know what is the suggestion that's being made to this witness. At the moment it is wholly unclear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: What is -- the only contestation, that there is first is, that he's speaking of prison and Madam Fauveau is speaking of hospital and not prison.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I thought we'd cleared this up.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think that has been cleared up. And then it's a question of dates, as far as I can see it. But how important, I don't know. I mean, it's -- yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What is quite clear is that the witness was in hospital physically. On the other hand, the witness say that is he was a prisoner at the hospital. I'm saying he was not a prisoner. He was not at the prison in Tunjice. He was simply in hospital. I'm going to move on to another subject, but --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I would suggest --

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But for the transcript, I object to what is being done with these documents. I contest the authenticity of these documents. Your Honour, can we have a pause, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. What do you need the pause for?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Between your questions and answers in the same language. I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Because the interpretation was as if you were asking me for a pause.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter. I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Do you need these documents, apart from the two we saw yesterday? I suppose there is only one of the other documents that the witness has come up with today that may be relevant, and that's the document that he was given in Banja Luka on the basis of which --

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The visa.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, exactly. These he only got when he was in Croatia. That, I understand has some relevance and the rest -- do you want it.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So we'll stick to the document that the witness said is basically a visa that he got while he was still in Banja Luka which enabled him to enter Croatia. I don't know which one it is. I mean, he's the one to indicate it to us.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It was certified by the police station in Novska. It says on -- so on it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Just pick it up -- no, no, the photocopy is what interests us. And the original you can keep. Have you identified the one, Madam Registrar? Shall we mark it DT20, Madam Fauveau?

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So that's being admitted as DT20. And please let's proceed. You may proceed. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: After you left the hospital, you went to Croatia; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: GRGO STOJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But I spent three days first of all in Caritas in Banja Luka.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: And when you were in Croatia, you didn't know that proceedings had been instituted against the perpetrator of the crime of which you were a victim.

utterances.speaker: GRGO STOJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what I heard.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: But you would not have returned to Republika Srpska to give testimony in the trial of the perpetrators of the crime of which you were a victim, even if you had been called to; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: GRGO STOJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I didn't want to deliver myself into their hands again.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: But you were the only survivor of this crime.

utterances.speaker: GRGO STOJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And I can see that in that document that there were two indicted by the military court in Banja Luka. I'm not mentioned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: The question of Madam Korner implied that you -- of Madam Fauveau implied that you were summoned -- you were called to give evidence in those proceedings. Were you effectively called, summoned to give evidence? Did you ever receive a summons, a call to give evidence?

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That was your question.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, that wasn't my question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Your question was: "But you can't return to Republika Srpska to give evidence in the trial of the perpetrators of the crime of which you were a victim, although you had been called to; is that correct?"

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. That -- my question would be: [In English] [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I was quite surprised by the translation because that's what I understood Madam Fauveau to be saying, "even if you had been called, you wouldn't come back."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Oh, I see. I wasn't following --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I saw the translation, so I thoughts I had misunderstood.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I wasn't following the French this time. So you never received the summons. Because yesterday, actually you were putting the argument that he couldn't have, because there were no --

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Exactly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I didn't receive any sort of summons, and I wasn't informed about this, so there's no point to discuss this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Madam Fauveau.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: A few minutes ago you said that even if you had received a summons, you wouldn't have gone to Republika Srpska; is that true?

utterances.speaker: GRGO STOJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, it wasn't until 1993 that Republika Srpska was recognised by the International Community. And I had reached Croatia by 1992 already. And when I left the prison, the hospital, Mrs. Nada came to me and helped me. She helped get me out, and she told me in these words, "You can't go to Sanski Most."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. So that's the end of the story. Next question.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: As the only survivor, you are in fact the key witness of this event; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: GRGO STOJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's why I'm here before this venerable Court.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know - and answer only if you do know - whether the prosecutor of the military tribunal summoned you as a witness? If he had summoned you as a witness, this case would never have taken place in Republika Srpska because you wouldn't have gone there.

utterances.speaker: GRGO STOJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that I had never been summoned.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: I'm not going to insist on this question.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the registrar show the witness document Exhibit P811.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: Is this a record from the investigative judge of the Sanski Most court dated the 3rd of November, 1992?

utterances.speaker: GRGO STOJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This isn't a record. This is a certificate which I submitted --

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: I apologise. I think the exhibit in question is P812.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 12. It was my fault.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: Is this a report from the investigating judge of the Sanski Most court dated the 3rd of November, 1992?

utterances.speaker: GRGO STOJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a report from the Sanski Most health centre which examined corpses. Dr. Prosic -- Ljiljana Prosic, medical specialist, examined the corpses.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We saw that document yesterday.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: You are right. You are quite right. And this report was addressed to the Sanski Most court, to the investigating judge.

utterances.speaker: GRGO STOJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that. I wasn't in Sanski Most. I was expelled.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: Doesn't this document mention the person it was sent to on the first page, at the top and to the left?

utterances.speaker: GRGO STOJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says "the lower court. Investigating judge." But who received it -- there's no stamp, no signature. There's no number saying where it was received.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: That's also true. But it's a document which belongs to the prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: GRGO STOJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But this is from the health centre.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: And in this report -- in this report the death of nine persons was established; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: GRGO STOJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: Some of these persons were killed during the same crime in which you were wounded; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: GRGO STOJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were all killed, but not when I was wounded. But five of them, at that point in time, and four of them when I was getting out. What's important is the crime took place on the same day.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You explained that yesterday.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: And for each of these persons, the doctor established the exact cause of death; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: GRGO STOJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm going to have a look -- I have to have a look then. That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: So the Serbian authorities did establish that this crime took place.

utterances.speaker: GRGO STOJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to the document, yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yesterday you said that the Serbs started treating the Croats different as of 1990, when the elections took place. That was on page 29 of the LiveNote. Did you mean to say that the relations between the Croats and Serbs deteriorated from 1990 onwards?

utterances.speaker: GRGO STOJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the Prosecutor show the witness the statement given to the Office of the Prosecutor in August 2000.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: Sir, could you have a look at page 2 of this statement. It's also page 2 in the English version. It's a sentence in the middle of the page. You said: [In English] "Relationships between the Serbs and the Croats living in Skrljevita were fine until the war."

utterances.speaker: GRGO STOJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: By that I meant up to the parliamentary elections. I can't remember every word. I can't memorise every word in my head. You have to understand what I've been through, what I've suffered.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So for you the elections and the war, there's no difference between the two.

utterances.speaker: GRGO STOJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Elections are one thing. War is another thing.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: But yesterday you said that the relations deteriorated after the elections. And in your statement, you said that they deteriorated just before the war. Between the war and the elections -- one year and a half passed between the war and the elections.

utterances.speaker: GRGO STOJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's how it was in my village. People in the neighbouring village behaved like that towards us. They didn't respond to the elections. They didn't go to the polling station in Skrljevita. The 26 of them -- the 26 Serbs who lived in the village of Skrljevita. The posters bothered them, the posters of the HDZ. They would pull them down, tear them down. Then they would try to find out where the meetings were being held.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That's not important for us to know. Forget it. Next question, Madam Fauveau.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: These Serbs from Skrljevita who didn't come to vote in the polling station that you went to, where did they go to vote?

utterances.speaker: GRGO STOJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't go to control that.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: Isn't it possible that these 26 Serbs who lived in a Croatian village, isn't it possible that they didn't go to vote because they were afraid?

utterances.speaker: GRGO STOJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know whether they were afraid, but what is important is the fact that they didn't want to go and vote. What they did before, until the first multi-party elections took place, they would come to the village -- they did this without any problem before. They would come to the village to collect the post, et cetera, and even children would go to Skrljevita to primary school. There were no problems at all.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yesterday you spoke about the Serbs who apparently returned to the front -- from the front in Croatia. You said that they went to the front in Croatia on a voluntary basis.

utterances.speaker: GRGO STOJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: Wasn't there demobilisation in 1991 -- a mobilisation in 1991?

utterances.speaker: GRGO STOJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, in 1991 there was a mobilisation. I was in Urosevac, in the army at the time.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: Why do you say that these Serbs left -- went to Croatia on a voluntary basis?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yeah. One moment. There has been --

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's mobilisation, Your Honour. [In English] It's mobilisation and not demobilisation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But I think it was -- I think it was translated correctly in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: In that case, since there was a mobilisation, why did you say that the Serbs left for Croatia -- went to Croatia on a voluntary basis?

utterances.speaker: GRGO STOJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When the first mobilisation occurred, the legal mobilisation, then the Croats responded to it too. When it stopped -- but they kept their weapons and their uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: My question related to the depart for Croatia.

utterances.speaker: GRGO STOJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I answered that question.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: So they didn't go there on a voluntary basis. They were mobilised.

utterances.speaker: GRGO STOJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Did I say that there was a demobilisation but that they remained in their uniforms and they kept their uniforms. They kept their weapons.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: In that case, they were -- they no longer belonged to the army at that point in time.

utterances.speaker: GRGO STOJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, what then?

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: If they had been demobilised --

utterances.speaker: GRGO STOJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: -- How can a demobilised person be under the orders of the army?

utterances.speaker: GRGO STOJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: So how could it be called an army then.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yeah. But this is becoming a cross-debate between the Defence -- counsel and the witness. He has already answered the question. He said that they didn't say there were a demobilisation but that they remained in their uniforms and they kept their uniforms. They kept their weapons. So that's clear enough. And one can argue on the basis of his reply later on, but not in a cross-debate with the witness. So next question.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, he didn't say that they were demobilised but he said that the mobilisation had been stopped. But in Serbo-Croat he said that they had been demobilised.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: What did you say? Can you explain to us in plain language what you said. Because if this is a question of interpretation, we have to clarify it.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I said that there was a demobilisation and that the Serbs kept their uniforms and their weapons.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That's it. He's answered you. And it's the same answer that he has -- he had given you before.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But my question --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yeah. But why -- why do you want the witness to tell you what that means or what the consequences -- you argue that when you come to the arguments stage.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And whether -- whether by being demobilised and you retain your uniform and your weapon, you are still a soldier or not a soldier is a submission -- can become a submission, if you want to resort to that submission. But don't expect -- I mean, if he tells me yes or if he tells me no, that's his own subjective opinion, and it's not -- it's not an expert opinion in any case.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: You spoke about Serbian checkpoints and you said that certain Serbs who were at these checkpoints were in civilian clothing, whereas others were wearing uniforms; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: GRGO STOJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: And you said that some men who were wearing uniform belonged to the reserve forces. When you say "the reserve force," are you referring to the Territorial Defence?

utterances.speaker: GRGO STOJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Territorial Defence; it could be. But it depends on how you define that.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yesterday you spoke about weapons which had been collected in your village and taken to Sanski Most. You said that these weapons were taken to Sanski Most to the Crisis Staff where the headquarters of the Serbian armed forces were located; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: GRGO STOJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: When you spoke about the Serbian armed forces, were you thinking of the SOS forces?

utterances.speaker: GRGO STOJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Serbian ground forces. SOS is the abbreviation for that.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yesterday you were speaking about -- you spoke about a meeting that took place in Kruhari. Bono, Ilija, and Ivica Tutic had been called to this meeting, and Tomo Delic was present there too.

utterances.speaker: GRGO STOJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: And you said that a soldier attended this meeting; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: GRGO STOJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: One officer. That's what Bono said. He was at the meeting. This is what I heard from him, from Bono. I didn't see it myself.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: So you personally didn't see this soldier.

utterances.speaker: GRGO STOJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wasn't at the meeting, so I couldn't see him in Kruhari.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you. Mr. Trbojevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRBOJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRBOJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Stojic, as a person I am really very sorry for what you went through. I have to say that I admire the courage that you have shown from the moment you were wounded until you were taken care of in hospital.

utterances.speaker: GRGO STOJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Thank you for those kind words at least.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRBOJEVIC
utterances.text: I think that is only to be expected from any normal human being.

utterances.speaker: GRGO STOJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is what I think it should be.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRBOJEVIC
utterances.text: I only have a few questions for you. On the first page of the statement you gave to the Prosecution, you said -- you spoke about the fact that in those days you followed political events in the country, that you remember the plebiscite at which the Serb people stated their position.

utterances.speaker: GRGO STOJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRBOJEVIC
utterances.text: But that you don't remember too well the contents of the plebiscite.

utterances.speaker: GRGO STOJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is right.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRBOJEVIC
utterances.text: But that essentially it had to do with whether the Serbs wanted to be a part of a -- some kind of new Yugoslavia with Krajina in Bosnia-Herzegovina and/or with the Krajinas in Croatia.

utterances.speaker: GRGO STOJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRBOJEVIC
utterances.text: If I ask you to read Exhibit DB88 --

utterances.speaker: MR. TRBOJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And could the usher please be so kind as to give it to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRBOJEVIC
utterances.text: I hope this document will remind you of that plebiscite. You call it a referendum, but in fact those words are synonymous. This is the Official Gazette, the Serbian Official Gazette. And in the top corner, it says "Decision on the adoption of the report," et cetera, et cetera. If you don't mind, will you please read point 2, "It is hereby established."

utterances.speaker: GRGO STOJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's not very well legible. It's not very legible.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRBOJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could you please give the witness my copy, which has been highlighted, so it's easier to read.

utterances.speaker: GRGO STOJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "It is hereby established that the decision for the Serbian people --"

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated].

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Just read it for yourself and to yourself. You don't need to read it aloud. And then we'll see what the question is. When you are ready, tell us please. Yes. Your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRBOJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TRBOJEVIC
utterances.text: Is it true that it is a decision of the Serbian people in Bosnia and Herzegovina to remain in Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: GRGO STOJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a decision on a plebiscite on the 9th and 10th of November, due to be held on those days in 1991, and when it was held indeed. And that came into effect -- has come into force.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRBOJEVIC
utterances.text: My question is whether it is clear from that text that it is a decision of the Serbian people in Bosnia-Herzegovina to remain in Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: GRGO STOJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is right. That is what it says. But on the ballot paper, the question wasn't like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRBOJEVIC
utterances.text: The question had to be word by word like that. My next question is: At that plebiscite, was it possible for other citizens, that is, members of other ethnic groups in Bosnia-Herzegovina to vote?

utterances.speaker: GRGO STOJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that. I was in the army at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRBOJEVIC
utterances.text: But you said that in the army, they took you to vote.

utterances.speaker: GRGO STOJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is right.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRBOJEVIC
utterances.text: Do you remember that there were ballot papers in two different colours?

utterances.speaker: GRGO STOJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRBOJEVIC
utterances.text: Very well. We'll move on to another subject. On page 4 of your statement to the Office of the Prosecutor, you said that upon your return from the army, you noticed that people of Serb ethnicity were more or less -- were armed. And there's a sentence that I would like to quote. And as for other citizens who received weapons, we know nothing about that." Do you remember saying something like that?

utterances.speaker: GRGO STOJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRBOJEVIC
utterances.text: Does it logically follow from that that there were other citizens who were armed as well?

utterances.speaker: GRGO STOJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that. I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRBOJEVIC
utterances.text: You told us that people of Serb ethnicity organised checkpoints.

utterances.speaker: GRGO STOJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRBOJEVIC
utterances.text: Did citizens of other ethnic groups organise guards or patrols in their villages?

utterances.speaker: GRGO STOJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not in my village.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRBOJEVIC
utterances.text: But did you hear about other villages?

utterances.speaker: GRGO STOJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not hear. I didn't go to other villages to check.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRBOJEVIC
utterances.text: Very well. But let us go back to the hospital for a moment, please. I think that it is -- that there is no dispute over the fact that at the time you were in hospital, there was a war going on and that the consequences of the war could be felt in the town of Banja Luka as well. Were there days with no electricity?

utterances.speaker: GRGO STOJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRBOJEVIC
utterances.text: When there was no -- there were no medical supplies.

utterances.speaker: GRGO STOJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRBOJEVIC
utterances.text: Do you know that HVO soldiers upon withdrawing from Travnik were put up in that same hospital?

utterances.speaker: GRGO STOJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not see them.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRBOJEVIC
utterances.text: You couldn't see them because you had left already by then, but you probably had read about it in the press. You didn't hear about it?

utterances.speaker: GRGO STOJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRBOJEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Is there re-examination?

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Stojic, I want to make sure that you have been returned all the documents that you showed us. Just make sure first that you have --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour, I have.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you. And this brings us to the end of your testimony here. And on behalf of the Chamber and everyone here, may I thank you for having come here to give evidence. You will be escorted out of this courtroom. And it is now possible for you to return to where you wish to go. Once more, I thank you. And you may now leave the room. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. And thank you for giving me this opportunity to speak about the truth that I personally experienced. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Good afternoon to you. And have a safe journey back home.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: The next witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] Does Your Honour want to start the witness before having a break? Or do you want a break now?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Sorry. My microphone. I have to tell Your Honour that was supposed to be one of the shorter witnesses.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I have to tell Your Honour that was supposed to be a short witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I know.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Would Your Honour like me to start the witness before the break?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I -- we start now, I think because of logistics I'm being advised yes, we start, and we'll break.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Can I just tell Your Honours two things: Firstly, we were able to provide the translation of the witness statement into B/C/S by the end of yesterday afternoon, so the defendants both have it. And we've had a translation done of the extra notebook, which I think, Your Honours -- the Defence have got it. We can provide it if necessary to Your Honours. Can I emphasise those the translations were not done by authorised translators. So if there's any problem, they will have to go to authorised translators.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's hope not.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And finally, can I just mention in relation to the documents that were shown to the witness relating to the non-prosecution, as it were, of --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Kajtez.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: The perpetrator, Kajtez, all those documents were supplied to us by the Republika Srpska authorities, the Banja Luka military court at a -- at a request. Those documents come from a source, which if the Defence want to suggest is not a source they -- on which we can rely, then ...

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We are not contesting those documents. It is the witness who contested them.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... Mr. Zulic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Again, we don't have any protective measures in place here, Ms. Korner. No?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I'm sorry?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We don't have any protective measures in place here.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: No, we don't.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Pardon me for asking you, because I just want to make sure because sometimes the situation changes from day to day.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour is quite right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And before jumping into and mentioning names, I always try to be as cautious as I can. Is there a problem? Do you have a problem?

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Mr. President. Just a small consultation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Zulic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: The gentleman standing next to you, who is the court usher, is going to give you a piece of paper on which there is the text of a solemn declaration to say the truth and nothing but the truth, which is required of you under our Rules. So before you start giving evidence, please take that document in your hand and read out that declaration aloud, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you. You may sit down. I'll explain very briefly what's going to happen. You're here to give evidence. You've been summoned to give evidence by the Prosecution in this case. The three persons you see up here, we form this Trial Chamber. I am the Presiding Judge. My name is Agius. I come from Malta. To my right is Judge Janu from the Czech Republic; so my right, Judge Taya from Japan. We will be the Chamber that will ultimately decide this -- this trial. To your right is the team -- on the front row is the team for the Prosecution. And today the Prosecution will start with a series of questions which they will put to you. When the Prosecution finishes with all the questions that it requires to put to you, you will then be cross-examined by the two teams -- two Defence teams that we have here. The first Defence team that you see in the front row to your left, the first three persons are the Defence team for the accused Radoslav Brdjanin. At the other end of the front row is the -- is counsel for General Talic. The three persons you see in front of you here are the members of the Registry. And you don't need to bother about the rest. No offence meant. It's not important for you to know who the others are. I mean, they are members of my legal team. You know, so it's not -- they have got nothing as such to do with the running of the case -- of the proceedings today. Who is going to cross-examine the witness?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Well, I hope I'm not going to cross-examine my own witness. But I'm calling --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Who is going to examine?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I am, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You are.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Ms. Korner from the -- for the Prosecution will be putting some questions to you. Thank you. I am afraid I don't think we will finish today, which means that you will have to return to The Hague to continue your evidence later on. I suppose this has been explained to him. I suppose this has been explained to you, and I'm sure you understand.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So Ms. Korner, the witness is in your hands.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] Mr. Zulic, is your name --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Mike, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Mr. Zulic, is your name Ahmet Zulic?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And were you born on the 5th of June, 1947 in Podbrijezje?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Which is in the Sanski Most municipality.

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And are you by ethnicity and religion a Muslim, now called Bosniak?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I'd like you first of all, if I may, to look at a map which is 7. -- 757.3. And I'm going to ask it to be put on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I'm going to give the witness my copy, because I've highlighted the village. I think one needs to go on the ELMO. He needs to have it himself. All right. I'm sorry, usher, you're quite right. You take my copy.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Usher.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: You take my copy. It's easier to see. And if you just put it on the ELMO and show it to the witness. You'll see it's marked there.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. Mr. Zulic, could you just look there. And you'll be just -- and just indicate where I have marked just below -- we can see -- it's actually -- where we see the town of Sanski Most, can we see the village in which you were born just to the left and marked, and where you lived in fact?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC
utterances.text: Could I please approach the map.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: That's where --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. For the record, the witness points at a village -- at a spot on the map which corresponds to the name Podbrijezje.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I'm glad that Your Honour has the same difficulty I do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think it's worse. I'm even worse.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Some I can do. But ones with "J's" in the middle, I can't. Yes, thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And just above that -- because we're going to refer to that later, Mr. Zulic -- is there a place called Podlug?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC
utterances.text: Yes. I showed it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. For the record, the witness points at the mentioned village on the map immediately on -- above the previous name.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Yes, you can take the map away.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Zulic. Now, Mr. Zulic, before we come to what actually happened to you in 1992, can we just deal with various statements and documents. In April of 2000, were you seen by an investigator from the Office of the Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC
utterances.text: Could you repeat the year, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: April of 2000 were you seen by an investigator?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Who spoke to you and recorded what you said. But at that stage you didn't sign a statement.

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC
utterances.text: I did not.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And were you then seen on a second occasion by another investigator? That was in February of 2001.

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And at that stage, did you provide to that investigator copies of effectively a diary that you had made after your release from Manjaca?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And later that year, last year in June, did the investigator return and at that stage was a signed statement taken from you?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: In addition, yesterday did you provide to the Office of the Prosecutor a -- a sort of little notebook on which you had written notes whilst you were in Manjaca?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: When you came to this Tribunal - I can't remember when it was now; I think on Monday, but - did you have a chance to read through a copy of the statement that you made to the investigator which had been translated into your own language, the Bosnian language?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And did you then make some minor corrections, I think, to spellings of names and some other words which had -- the translation wasn't altogether correct?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Now, can I just ask you, please, about the diary that you wrote after your release from Manjaca. I think it's right -- have you got with you the original, which is a set of three notebooks?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC
utterances.text: I didn't bring it just now, but it's at the hotel. I didn't believe it was necessary now.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: It may not, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: But you have them available and you can make them available on the next occasion you come here; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC
utterances.text: If necessary, you can send someone to pick up the key of my room and to bring it.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Don't worry, Mr. Zulic. Now, can you just tell the Court when did you actually write the account of the events that are contained in those exercise books.

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC
utterances.text: After Christmas in 1992 until the 15th or 20th of January, 1993.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And what made you decide to write this account of the events that happened to you?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC
utterances.text: Just so that it would be never forgotten.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Did you write your account of events at anybody else's suggestion?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC
utterances.text: On my own.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Did anybody ask you to write down what had happened to you?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC
utterances.text: Not to write down, but they did ask me for a statement and I wouldn't give it to them.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And who was it who asked you for a statement?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC
utterances.text: Mr. Adil Draganovic did.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And you said that you wouldn't give a statement to Judge Draganovic. Why was that?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC
utterances.text: Because I was afraid. My father and mother remained in Bosnia; also two brothers, their wives and children. And I was afraid of any publication. Because if that were to be learnt, they would certainly be killed.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And was this the situation, that you and Judge Draganovic had been released from Manjaca together?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And that you were housed in the same barracks in Germany for a period of a month or so before you moved on?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: When you wrote your account of the events that you describe --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Sorry. [Microphone not activated] But I have a sign an order before 4.00 --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Mike, please, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: The legal assistants --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I see. I can just finish this question, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. I'm sorry to interrupt you like that, but I know that the Registry closes at 4.00.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And so I've only got five minutes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, just one simple question.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: When you wrote the account of events, Mr. Zulic, in your notebooks, were those events still fresh in your memory?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, Ms. Korner. We'll have a 30-minute break, and then we'll continue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] Questions should be --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour may have seen, I got a message during the course of cross-examination. I just wish I'd seen it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] I say this is the first --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: This is the first World Cup that I'm missing.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Mr. Zulic, just one last question about the diary. Until you provided a copy of it to the investigator, had you shown that diary to anyone else?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC
utterances.text: To no one, apart from my family, my son, my wife. They knew about it.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Well, when we have a look at it, we'll see what you wrote on the front cover.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, may I say that I'm going to ask, when we get to the point, that the witness be given the photocopies -- I'm going to ask it be made an exhibit and then if necessary, I'm going to ask him to refresh his memory from what he wrote, nearer the time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Do you have any objections? Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And sir, I think it -- Mr. Zulic, I think it's right that you were born and raised and have spent most of your life within the municipality of Sanski Most.

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Other than when you did your military service.

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Did you work until 1992 for a coal mining firm in a place called Dosci?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And were you in fact by may -- in May of 1992 the manager of production?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC
utterances.text: Not the manager, but I was a supervisor -- the director supervisor. I supervised the shifts in the pit.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. Now, I don't think that you were ever a member of a political party of any kind.

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC
utterances.text: Never.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And took no interest in politics.

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC
utterances.text: Neither before nor today.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: However, in -- you were aware, were you not, that in 19 -- after the 1990 elections, the president of the municipal assembly was a man -- or became a man named Nedeljko Rasula?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And I think you knew Rasula because he was your teacher, both in elementary and high school.

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Now, I want to come directly, please, to the events of 1991 -- the end of 1991 and 1992. By the end of 1991, were checkpoints appearing in the municipality of Sanski Most?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC
utterances.text: Yes, they were.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And I think towards the -- after -- I'm sorry. In the period of 1991, every person of all ethnicities were stopped. But did that change in 1992?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC
utterances.text: In April, yes, it did, in my opinion.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And change was what?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC
utterances.text: Well, among those police, there were no longer -- it was the military police, and there were no longer Muslims among them. And if they stopped Serbs, they wouldn't check them; they would just let them go. But they would check the Muslims. They would check their cars. And that happened to me a few times.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Now, did you notice that appearing in 1992 were different kinds of military units?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And what kind of units were -- began to appear in the Sanski Most area?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC
utterances.text: There was the JNA, some "White Eagles," Seselj's men, the SOS -- that must have been the Serbian armed forces -- and some other paramilitary formations, private military in fact, which I had never seen before. I really haven't.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: You've described some as the White Eagles, Seselj's men. How did you know these people were called the White Eagles and were Seselj's men?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC
utterances.text: Because they would say so publicly. That was said publicly. They had a white band here. I can't remember exactly whether it was on the -- on their left or right arm. They had cockades here.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And the SOS, did you know who was the leader of the SOS?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC
utterances.text: At the time, they said it was Njunja and Medeni. Dusan Saovic, that's the man. And Medeni, I really don't know his real name.
