utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Now, do you remember the occasion when the municipal building was attacked in Sanski Most?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC
utterances.text: At the moment, I can't remember the date. I have it written down somewhere. But I know it was sometime in May.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. Don't worry about the date. We've got documents that is show us the date. And do you remember that what was called a War Presidency or Crisis Staff was set up in the municipality?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC
utterances.text: The Crisis Staff was formed in April. It had already been formed then.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, I want to deal with the matter of weapons. Did you, at some stage, in 1992, purchase a weapon?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Roughly when was that?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC
utterances.text: I think it was in March. I haven't got the dates in front of me, but it was in 1992 before April.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And how did you come -- well, first of all, from whom did you purchase the weapon?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC
utterances.text: From a Serbian soldier. I paid for it, purchased it.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And what sort of weapon was it?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC
utterances.text: It was a light machine-gun with 20 bullets.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And what was the reason that you decided to buy a weapon?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC
utterances.text: Well, you could see that there was a war. It was necessary to protect one's family.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: For how long did you keep that weapon?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC
utterances.text: Until about May 1992.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And what -- and what did you do with it in May of 1992?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC
utterances.text: I threw it into a well.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And why did you do that?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC
utterances.text: Well, you can't do anything with 20 bullets, even if you were to try and protect your family.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Was that before or after there had been announcement that all weapons were to be handed in to the authorities?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC
utterances.text: That was before.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Now, do you recall if announcements over the radio ordering people to hand in their weapons?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And when that announcement was made, did the people who lived in your village surrender their weapons?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC
utterances.text: Yes, they did. The ones that they owned privately, the pistols and the hunting rifles, and other weapons that had been obtained.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And I should have asked you this earlier. Roughly how big was your village? How many families?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC
utterances.text: About 380 houses. That's the number.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And how were the weapons handed in? Did somebody collect them for the whole village, or did people hand them in individually?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC
utterances.text: No. They came to the village. They said that they would collect it in front of the centre. Dragan Acic came and another two soldiers who collected those weapons, and everything was surrendered.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And who was Dragan Acic?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC
utterances.text: He's a citizen from Sanski Most. He was wearing a military uniform. He was wearing a JNA uniform. He was a reserve captain, a sergeant or a captain, something like that.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And you say that everything was surrendered. So were there any weapons left in your village?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC
utterances.text: Well, maybe some were left. I don't know really.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Now, before the weapons were handed in, were there any patrols being conducted by the Muslim population in the village?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC
utterances.text: Yes, there were.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And was the whole village Muslim, or was it ethnically mixed?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC
utterances.text: The whole village was Muslim.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: What was the reason that patrols were being carried out?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC
utterances.text: I have to explain that. The people from Podlug, the Serbs, they came, and they said that Muslims would be patrolling independently and the Serbs independently, so as to avoid extremists coming in, being inserted.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: So the village of Podlug, which we looked at the map earlier --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment, Ms. Korner. Yes, Mr. Ackerman.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm just wondering if the witness would be more comfortable if he could move his chair a little forward. Because I think that he's leaning forward every time he speaks and I think sometimes he doesn't quite get forward and I don't think he's being heard quite as well as he would otherwise be. Just a helpful suggestion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. If you move further near the microphone, it would be better. Yes, Ms. Korner.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Ackerman.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Sir, yes. We were just asking -- the village of Podlug which we looked at, was that a Serb village entirely?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC
utterances.text: Yes. There were three Muslim houses in that village.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And you say that the villagers from there came to your village and said that there should be separate patrols, Serb patrols for Podlug and Muslim for your village; is that right?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: After you'd had to surrender your weapons - you, the Muslims - did you conduct any further patrols?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC
utterances.text: With what and how?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes, quite. So is the answer no?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: What about the Serbs in Podlug? Did they surrender their weapons?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC
utterances.text: No, they didn't.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And did they continue with the patrols?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC
utterances.text: Yes, they did.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Now, you told us about -- that you had this job at the mining company. Were you able to keep your job?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC
utterances.text: No, I wasn't.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: What happened to you, in respect of your employment?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC
utterances.text: We went to work. And after we had done a shift, we went out. The bus didn't come to get us, and we were told by the people at the door that we had to leave the company. And I would like to emphasise that up until then only Muslims worked there from March up until the middle of April. I have that written down in my diary. Only Muslims worked there, whereas the Serbs had already been deployed, sent off to certain units.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: So at what stage were you told -- can you remember roughly the date when you were told that you had to leave the company?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC
utterances.text: It was in May.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Now --

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC
utterances.text: At the beginning of May.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Now, I want to come to the events of late May of 1992. Did you hear announcements on the radio talking about what were called "Green Berets"?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And were people named whom you knew?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC
utterances.text: The people whom I knew were mentioned -- they were told to come, to surrender to the Serbian people. They were told that they were extremists, because the Green Berets, as they call them, they're all over the place.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC
utterances.text: They said.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And what did you understand was being referred to by the term "Green Berets"?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC
utterances.text: Believe me, at the time I didn't -- and even today I don't know if those are those green caps. But at the time I didn't see anything like that.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Green caps. But people wore green caps. But who were these people who wore green caps supposed to be?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You can put a direct question, Ms. Korner. Straight away. Go straight to it.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, there may be some dispute about this. But in any event if Your Honour tells me I can, I will.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Did you understand they were referring to armed Muslim males?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Now, were you ever aware of any armed Muslim forces in Sanski Most itself?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC
utterances.text: No, I wasn't.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: In your own village?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Or any other Muslim areas in which you travelled?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC
utterances.text: At that point in time, no. But later on I heard that that was in Vrhpolje, somewhere up there.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And that's -- I'm dealing now with the announcement on the radio. And was that announcement on the 26th of May of 1992 or thereabouts?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC
utterances.text: Thereabouts, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Now, after that announcement when people were named, was there any outbreak of firing or any kind of warfare?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC
utterances.text: Not in my village. In Vrhpolje, I heard that there was fighting.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Now, I want to ask you about the area of Sanski Most called Mahala. Were you familiar with that area?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC
utterances.text: Yes, I was very familiar with it.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Can you tell us what happened to the people who lived in Mahala.

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC
utterances.text: They were called over the announcement. They were asked to leave their houses. Some of them were asked to go to the village Krkojevci, to the stadium, and others were asked to go to the training ground where there were driving courses so that the Serbian forces could deal with the Green Berets. And they did that.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Okay. So this is what was being said. "They were asked to leave their houses, and some of them were asked to go to a village called Krkojevci, to a stadium, others to the training ground."

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC
utterances.text: To the stadium in the village of Krkojevci and above Muhici to the training ground.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And you said "so that the Serbian forces could deal with the Green Berets." Is that what they were saying on the radio?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I'm sorry. Could we -- could you just have a look, again, please at the Map.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: If we can put that on the ELMO, and if we put my marked copy again. Yes. If you could move the map up the screen, please. Yes. Yes, that's it. Fine. Stop. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Is that the village of Krkojevci, which you're referring to?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC
utterances.text: This is the village of Krkojevci.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. For the record the witness points at the name "Krkojevci" on the map.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes, thank you. You can take the map back again. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Now, having heard this announcement, did the people in the area of Mahala obey it?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC
utterances.text: They went out. Some of them went to Krkojevci and the others went to the training ground.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: How do you know that's what they did?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC
utterances.text: Because later on the refugees from Mahala and Muhici went up there, came there, and they told us where they had been, two or three days later.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: They came to your village.

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Now, did you see what happened to Mahala?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC
utterances.text: After the people had been forced out, I saw that houses had been destroyed. I saw that Mahala was being shelled. I saw smoke. I saw that there were houses burning, that they had been destroyed. We saw that because we were on an elevation.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Can we take this in stages. What was the first thing you actually saw happening? We're going to look at a film in a moment, but what was the first thing you saw happening?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC
utterances.text: We heard shooting. That's the first thing.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And what kind of shooting? Do you mean rifles or other guns?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC
utterances.text: Mortars. I think they were mortars. But there was shelling.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And once you heard what was happening, did you go and have a look?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC
utterances.text: No one could do that. No one dared do that.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: No. I'm sorry. I don't mean go into Mahala. But could you see where the firing was coming from?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC
utterances.text: It was very clear. It was quite possible to see where the firing came from. From the Djedovaca hill, from the garbage dump, and from the direction of Caplje. But a little below Caplje. It could be seen quite clearly. You could see the shells flying quite clearly. You would hear the sound it made. This was a very loud noise.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Now, what was the result that you could see of the shelling?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC
utterances.text: I think that some houses started burning immediately.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Could you see the mosque from your position?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Could you see what was happening to the mosque?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC
utterances.text: Not at that point in time.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Whilst you were watching, did you see any kind of people in Mahala returning fire, any kind of resistance to what was happening?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC
utterances.text: There was no resistance. I know that no one fired a shot.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Were there people still in Mahala at the time of the shelling?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC
utterances.text: Earlier on I said that they were all taken to the training ground and to the stadium in Krkojevci.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes. I understand that. But did you discover whether or not at the time of the shelling anybody had been left in the village?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC
utterances.text: If anyone remained in the village, then that was someone who was immobile, who couldn't move, sick people, or someone who had hidden in that person's house, in the cellar.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I think I should -- but do you know whether that happened or not? If you don't know, say so.

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC
utterances.text: I don't know whether people returned, fired. But I know the people remained in Mahala. Later on they were found and had been killed. These were -- they were mainly women. In my diary it says who these women were. There were three -- three men -- three or four men. In the house of Semir Hegic [phoen], in the cellar two brothers Vojnikovic were killed. Ivo Uzar, Nafira, who worked in the book shop --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: You needn't bother to list everybody, because, as you say, you've listed the names in your diary. Now, did -- did you yourself go to Mahala after the shelling had finished?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: After the shelling had finished, did anybody go into the village?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC
utterances.text: Women went back, but only after they had taken them to the school and then separated the men to the sports hall and then they sent the women to us in Podbrijezje, the children to Stari Majdan, and then women three days later went to Mahala.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: What happened to property that hadn't been damaged by the shelling for one reason or another?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC
utterances.text: It was looted and taken away, simply, because the women that went back there to get their clothes to change into or to bring flour or something like that mainly didn't find anything there. I had 18 refugees in my home.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And were the houses after they'd been looted, were they left, or did something happen to them?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC
utterances.text: No. Afterwards houses were burning every day, two, three, or four. This could be seen. One could see the smoke when the houses went up in flames.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Now, did your mother-in-law in fact live in the Mahala area?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And what happened to her?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC
utterances.text: She was expelled too, and she came to my place. She was first expelled to Krkojevci, the stadium there. And then in front of the Narodni Front School, when they killed my father-in-law. Then she managed to reach my house. My father-in-law at the time was 67 years old.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And who was responsible for killing your father-in-law?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC
utterances.text: The Serbs.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Was he the only one killed, or were others killed?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC
utterances.text: I just said a moment ago all the people who had been killed. But he was immobile; he couldn't move. May I correct myself. He wasn't killed. He was burnt in his house. He was bedridden. Sorry.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. In 1996, after your return to Sanski Most, did you go and film the area of Mahala as it was in 1996?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: We're going to -- I'm going to ask you to look at the film in a moment. But by that stage had some rebuilding already started?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: So I'm going to ask that that be played. But I think in addition, have you filmed the view that you had over your village of Mahala, which was filmed when the investigator was with you?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. I filmed it to show that I was able to see the burning of houses and the shelling that -- from where I stood.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. Your Honour, we've given the video to the audiovisual unit. It hasn't got an exhibit number yet. So the next one up will be Prosecutor's Exhibit 821. So I wonder if that could be played.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And, sir, if there's anything you want to comment on, if you could just say "stop" loudly, then the film will stop playing.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: No. I'm sorry. It's the wrong video. It's the other video that the visual -- audiovisual unit was given.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Stop. Wind back, please, a little. Here you can see a house that before the war --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Stop.

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC
utterances.text: -- was a coffee bar.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: If you stop for a moment. You can't indicate with the pointer to that screen. If you can just describe -- you say there was a coffee bar where? To the left or the right of the screen as we look at it?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC
utterances.text: To the right, as I see it. This was a coffee bar before the war. And to the left was the market.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Okay. Can we see anywhere the mosque or what was left of the mosque?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC
utterances.text: The mosques can't be seen. It was on the left. Behind the market there's a street there. Only this coffee bar was all in marble before the war.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: If we could continue playing.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: If we could just pause the camera there for a moment. It's rather difficult for pausing it.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: But what are we looking at there on the walls of the house?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC
utterances.text: You can see the scars left by shells, the damage left by shells.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Could we move on.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And what are we looking at here?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC
utterances.text: It is just here, behind this is the exercise ground that I referred to, the exercise area. And here you can see a part of the Serb area.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Now can we pause the film for a moment. Sorry.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Now, are we now looking at the view you had of Mahala from where you lived?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC
utterances.text: Yes, precisely so. If you go back a little, you can see the mosque very well too.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Okay. If we could just run the -- run the film back for a moment.

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC
utterances.text: This is the newly built mosque that we see.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yeah. It is not very clear on the screen, but we can see the two -- I'm not very sure what the name is?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC
utterances.text: Minarets.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Okay. And that's the newly built one, is it?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Okay. If we could just move on.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And if you could just indicate the hills from where the firing was coming when you see it.

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC
utterances.text: You can't see it too well, but you will see a hill over here to -- over there called Djedovaca, above the houses here.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I don't -- Your Honour, I've seen this film before, and it wasn't as bad as this. I'm just wondering whether the colour -- whether one can adjust the colour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] But I'm not quite sure.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Stop.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: What are we looking at there?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC
utterances.text: Now you can see clearly the Djedovaca hill. I can tell you this peak here to the left is what is known as Smedlista [phoen], and over there is the hill called Djedovaca.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I think -- well, let's just run the film on. I think that's nearly it though. Could we just run the film and see if that's the end.

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC
utterances.text: Over there to the left you can see a hill called Caplje, from where they were also firing.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you very much. That's it.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Now, what were the next things that happened before your arrest? Were any other areas attacked?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Which areas? And if you need your diary to assist you, sir, at this stage, you can have it. Would you prefer to have it, or can you remember without?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC
utterances.text: Perhaps I will be more precise if I have the diary as to which village came when.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Could I -- could you be hand --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm going to ask that the photocopy be made of the exhibit so that he can retain the original.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I'm going to ask that you get part 1 of your diary.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'll ask they all be exhibited as one single exhibit. But because there are three parts of it, three books, if we could have the first book as Exhibit -- where are we? -- 822.1. And --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I understand that the original is in your possession and readily available --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: It's in the possession of the witness. But he'll bring it back next time he comes to court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That's very important.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Because at any time we may need to refer to it.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes, I agree.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I'd just like you to be handed also this document, which is a photocopy of the front of the first exercise book.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, it's the one I handed out yesterday.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Zulic, is that a photocopy of the cover of the first exercise book?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And can you just read out to us what you wrote there.

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC
utterances.text: "Just so that our grandchildren do not forget."

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And I should ask you this, Mr. Zulic, or I should have asked you earlier. When you were writing the diary, did you write down everything in it that happened to you or other people?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And why not?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC
utterances.text: First of all, if I were to bring down everything, I was afraid I might poison the people for whom this was written.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] And --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Mike, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And who were you afraid that it might poison? Who were the people that you wrote it for?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC
utterances.text: For my grandchildren.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Now, if you find the part, sir -- in the first part of your diary where -- is that the first --

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC
utterances.text: No. I have book 3. That's why I'm looking.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes. Okay. We'll give you --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: It's that one.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Is that the first part of your diary?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: If you find the page -- well, first of all -- I'm sorry. Before we deal with the Sanski Most -- were you able to see the attack that took place on Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. Then perhaps you'd like to find the page in your diary - and I can't help you, I'm afraid - where you dealt with Hrustovo and Vrhpolje.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, that's page 3 of the translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Korner.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I don't know if any of the Defence could assist with where that passage is in the original to help the witness, so that we can ...

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is page 6.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] Thank you, Madam Fauveau.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Excuse me. I'm sorry. Page 7.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Have you found the passage, sir, where you deal with -- perhaps it would be quicker if I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I can indicate to him. Sir, you have the diary, the photocopies. And you see that each page has a number, eight digits.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Now, starting from the first one, you turn six pages and you come to the seventh page, which is 02005348. Go to the bottom of the page, and go up nine lines there from there. The line starts with [B/C/S spoken] Or something like that.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] On my page 6, I can't --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Your page 7 you have to go to. That's why I said you start with the first one, you turn six pages, and you come to page 7. And nine lines from the bottom.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Have you found that, Mr. Zulic?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I want to deal with this quite quickly. You record there the attack on Hrustovo and Vrhpolje where more than 300 civilians were killed. Were you able to see the attack, or did you hear about it afterwards?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC
utterances.text: I heard of this attack, because a woman came -- I think I noted that down somewhere.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes, you did.

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC
utterances.text: A woman came who --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Don't --

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC
utterances.text: -- who said -- she came to the yard of my neighbour Ibro's house, and he said -- and she said that in one garage --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC
utterances.text: -- 18 or 20 people had been killed, that on the bridge about 30 adult males had been executed, and that they continued executing in Vrhpolje, Hrustovo.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Sir, can I explain. We're going to hear from people who were actually present at these incidents. All I want to establish is how you found out about them. So somebody came and spoke to your neighbour. Were you present when that happened?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC
utterances.text: This woman told me who survived, in that garage. No.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I understand, sir. Don't worry. We actually are going to be hearing about that. But were you present when the woman who came from that area told your neighbour, or was it your neighbour who told you?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC
utterances.text: I was present. I was sitting there. She was sleeping in my house. Anyway, I was captured and taken away, and she stayed behind in my house.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Now, the refugees from Mahala who had been living in your house, what happened to them?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC
utterances.text: They tried to be transported to Jajce, the first time. The police went, the Serb police, with a loudspeaker in their hand, saying that all refugees should gather in Podbrijezje near the cultural centre and that they would go to Jajce.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And were they in fact taken to Jajce?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC
utterances.text: They were taken and brought back again.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And what happened -- I want to jump ahead. What happened to them eventually?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC
utterances.text: When they were brought back, some to Podbrijezje and some to Stari Majdan. After three days, there was another announcement that the refugees should gather and that they would be taken to Velika Kladusa. However, the refugees realised by now that they wanted to expel them, force them out of their houses, so they didn't want to go. However, they organised buses and the army, and the army or soldiers went from one house to the next searching the house, and wherever they found refugees in the house they would force them out. And those who couldn't fit into the buses were chased across the river to Krings Company, and new buses came and they were put on those buses and driven off in the direction of Kladusa.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And do you know what happened to these people eventually, where they went to?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC
utterances.text: They arrived in Kladusa.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And that's as much as you know.

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC
utterances.text: That's all I know.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Now, you've told us that it was Serb -- it was the army or soldiers who came and took these people from their houses, put them onto buses. Who do you mean by "the army"?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC
utterances.text: I mean those who had a five-coronet star here.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Were they regular soldiers as far as you could tell or irregular?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC
utterances.text: As far as I could tell, they were regular soldiers, but reservists. These were not young men but mostly older men. You know, between 35 and 40, something like that.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And do you know which unit of the regular army was operating in your area -- in that area?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC
utterances.text: The 6th Krajina Brigade. At least that is how they called it.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Now, can we just deal, please, with the attacks. And if we just deal with where they happened. Was there an attack on a village called Cirkici?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC
utterances.text: Cirkici, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And was that an entirely Muslim village again?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And was there then an attack on Skucani Vakuf?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC
utterances.text: Skucani Vakuf.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And was there then shelling of Trnovo?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Now, were you able -- Trnovo was in fact a village that was not that far away from you, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Were you able to see that attack?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC
utterances.text: Yes, I was. I could see the shells coming across the hill and falling into Trnovo.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And where was the shelling coming from?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC
utterances.text: From Djedovaca, from the garbage dump.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And anywhere else that you could see?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC
utterances.text: Yes. From Podlug, from the stadium there. There was also a Fap lorry, which had been converted, and they had mounted what they called a two-barreled anti-aircraft gun on it.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Now, you can leave the diary for a moment, sir, and we'll come back to it if necessary. During these attacks, from what you saw was there any response from the inhabitants of the village, any firing back?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC
utterances.text: They had nothing with which to fire back.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And why was that?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC
utterances.text: Well, as they had surrendered their weapons.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your village, did anything happen to that before your arrest?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And what happened to your village?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC
utterances.text: There was shelling. One shell fell in the -- in my father's garden, and the second shell about 300 metres further away in the garden of a neighbour of ours -- of mine. The one that fell in my father's garden didn't explode, and the one that fell further up did explode. And then we were told over the radio that we would be shelled.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Was there concentrated shelling on your village - in other words, more than one or two - before your arrest?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC
utterances.text: No, there wasn't. No.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I'm going to deal with your arrest in a moment, but was there -- after your arrest, was there any concentrated shelling on the village, or did it remain?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC
utterances.text: I heard that there was concentrated shelling on our village about one month later. This is what I was told by my wife and by my children.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. I want to now deal with your arrest, please. Did that take place on the 18th of June?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC
utterances.text: Yes, it did.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And did some police officers -- armed police officers arrive at your home?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC
utterances.text: Yes, they did.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Were there four of them in all?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And did you know them all as local Serbs?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And you recorded their names. Was there somebody called Gojko Macura?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And Predrag Maric?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Miroslav Mauna?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And the fourth man, I think who was also the driver, was he called Dosenovic? Maybe you'd better say it.

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC
utterances.text: Dosenovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Did they tell you that you were going to be taken for interrogation?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC
utterances.text: They told me that I should go and give a statement, and they asked me to give them weapons. They were looking for bomb, for grenades, for a sniper rifle, for a light machine-gun. They were looking for mortars.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Did they search your house?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC
utterances.text: Not at all.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: So they told you that you were going to have a give a statement, and they asked you to give them weapons. Did you tell them --

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: What did you tell them?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC
utterances.text: I told them that I didn't have any, and I told them I couldn't give them something that I didn't have. I told them that I had thrown something into a well and that they should go and have a look and see that it couldn't be taken out again.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Now, having -- well, I'm sorry, having told them that, what was their reaction?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC
utterances.text: They started hitting me, and they said, "You're going to come with us and you're going to give a statement."

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And where did they take you?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC
utterances.text: They took me to Betonirka.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And what was -- did you know what Betonirka was?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC
utterances.text: I knew that it was a company which produced concrete products.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Once you got to Betonirka, what happened to your possessions?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC
utterances.text: They started provoking my wife. Immediately they started phoning her. And this lasted I don't know for how long. But according to what my wife told me, it occurred almost every evening.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes. I'm sorry. It's my fault, sir. What happened to your personal property, what you had on you, once you got to the garage -- once you got to the Betonirka?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC
utterances.text: Everything was taken from me, money, my watch, my driving licence, my identity card. Everything was taken from me. And some other papers that I had in my wallet.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And was that taken from you by the people who had arrested you or by another policeman, or another person?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC
utterances.text: Other people.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: The people who arrested you, you say were policemen. When you got to Betonirka, were the people you were dealing with there policemen?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC
utterances.text: I don't know what they were, but they weren't wearing a regular civilian police uniform, as far as I could see.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: What were they wearing?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC
utterances.text: One of them was wearing an officer's uniform, an olive-drab uniform. Some of them were also wearing camouflage uniforms. And one or two of them were wearing those police uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Now, once you'd had your property removed from you, were you taken to what used to be the garages of the factory?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC
utterances.text: Yes, I was.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And were you placed into one of the garages?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC
utterances.text: Yes, in garage number 1, as they call it.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I'd like you to -- for a moment to be shown a plan with the photographs, which is Prosecutor's Exhibit P757.1.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] Now, Ms. Korner, this is --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. I pushed the wrong button. Ms. Korner, this document is already exhibited.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: For the future, always have available -- when you come forward with documents like the present with, with a map in the middle, flanked on the sides with photos -- one which does not indicate beneath each of the photos what that photo represents.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: You --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We leave it -- we leave it -- I have no qualms with having myself and the Defence with a map with the photos and the indication of what each photo represents. But I would rather prefer that the witness hasn't got any indications, and then he is asked to confirm whether the indication which is on the map is the right one or not. More or less this is to achieve a certain uniformity. And I'm sure you understand me. But I do personally also agree that ideally this is how it should be. Today we can go ahead with the document that we have, and I am pretty sure that what you are going to ask the witness is not going to be that much controversial. But for the future, please let's do it this way.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, may I say you don't take me entirely by surprise, having heard what's been happening in other Trial Chambers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: No. I was pretty sure that I was not going to take you by surprise.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, we'll make -- we'll try -- unfortunately these maps were prepared --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, I know.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: But we'll see what we can do about that.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All I'd like you to do, sir, is just could you look --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Usher, put it on the ELMO, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Could you just confirm that that's a photograph taken last year of the garages at Betonirka. But did it look like that in 1992?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: The technicians -- I don't know who is in charge of -- yes. Okay. Exactly. We're -- for the record, we are looking at photo number 1. And I thank the technicians for blowing that up. Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] These are the garages in photograph number 1.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And which garage were you placed in?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC
utterances.text: Garage number 1.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: For the record, the witness indicates the last door painted red at the right side of the photo.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you very much. You can take that away.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: When you got to your garage, were there already some 30 people inside it?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm going -- can I just say for the record, I'm going to lead -- and if either of the Defence want me to stop leading, then I'll do so.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Were there about 30 people in the garage?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC
utterances.text: Something like that. About 30.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And did that include people whom you recognised?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC
utterances.text: Yes, it did.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: One of whom was the Muslim commander of the -- ex-commander of the police, I suppose by then, Enver Burnic?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And were there -- did it also include at least one Croat from the village of Stara Rijeka?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC
utterances.text: Yes, Andjelko Skripa.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Now, was there sufficient room in the garage for you to sleep?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC
utterances.text: Usually not, because the garage was about 5 to 6 metres long and about 3 metres wide.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And what about ventilation?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC
utterances.text: We didn't have any ventilation. There was a window -- there were 30 or 40 of us in the garage, and they put concrete blocks against that window. So they closed it.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Now, were you taken to the police building, the SUP, for interrogation on the third day?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC
utterances.text: Yes, I was.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And what were you being asked about?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC
utterances.text: The questions they asked were who has weapons, what kind of weapon, why haven't you sold the weapons? But mostly it was who had weapons, what kind of weapons, how many Green Berets are there? The questions were mainly questions about who the extremists were. And at the end he told me, "You'll tell us about all of this and you'll confess. You'll go and dig out the well. You'll go and fish in the well and you'll take your weapon out of it, because the cat [RealTime transcript read in error "camp"] can eat you up in no time." Dusko Zoric questioned me, from Sahovci.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I'm sorry. Just pause for a moment what did you say? He said -- the man said you'll go and fish in the well and you'll go and take your weapon out of it because what can eat you up in no time?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC
utterances.text: The cat would eat me up in no time.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, it's come up at camp on the screen. That's why I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. It's camp on the screen. Now it's cat.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: It's come up as camp again. Exactly. But the witness is saying cat. And he is saying cat before. That's what I heard at least.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And what did you understand by the expression "the cat can eat you up in no time"?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC
utterances.text: I took that to mean that they would kill me.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Now, you told us who was asking you the questions. Did you know this man, Mr. Zoric?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Was he a policeman?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC
utterances.text: He was a lawyer.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Did anything happen to you during the questioning?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC
utterances.text: Not while he was questioning me, no.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Did anything happen to you after the questioning?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC
utterances.text: Nothing happened to me in the office. He didn't beat me. I think that he even behaved quite correctly at times. But when I was coming back down the stairs, before that he said, "Kravic, push him down the steps and hit him where you want to, so that he can be hurt wherever."

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: This is what Zoric said?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And what did happen once you left the office?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC
utterances.text: When I reached the stairs, he pushed me. He hit me with the rifle. And here I have a wound from that blow. If necessary, I can show it.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I don't think that will be necessary. I think we -- the Chamber is prepared to accept that. He pushed -- he hit you with a rifle, and what happened?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC
utterances.text: I fell down the stairs.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And were you able to get up, or did something further happen?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC
utterances.text: I had to stand up very quickly.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Now, was that the first time that you had been assaulted?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC
utterances.text: No. I'd been beaten earlier on too.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And when had that happened?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC
utterances.text: Before I went to the questioning.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Was -- and who -- who beat you?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC
utterances.text: The people on duty who were guarding us.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Now, during your imprisonment in Betonirka, how often were you beaten?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC
utterances.text: Well, I wasn't beaten only on three nights out of the 21 nights I spent in Betonirka.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: There were only three nights when you weren't beaten.

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC
utterances.text: Yes. At the time -- it was the shift of a certain policeman called Tolcin. It was his shift, and he opened the door of the garage. We were given water when he was on shift. We were also allowed -- we were even allowed to shave ourselves and to wash ourselves, so we could pour water over ourselves.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: So on those -- when that policeman was on duty, you weren't beaten. On every other night you were beaten.

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC
utterances.text: They didn't beat anyone when that policeman was on duty.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Right. I'm sorry. I just want you to confirm. Are you saying those are the only three nights when you were not beaten?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: What was used to beat you?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC
utterances.text: Sometimes they would beat with all sorts of things. Sometimes they would bring children in and they would train karate on us. Sometimes they did it for the sake of it. They didn't use all their force. Sometimes they used cables to beat us, they kicked us, they used the table -- feet of tables and they used sort of spades. They would hit us with those sort of things.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And did that happen to everyone who was in the -- the garage with you?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC
utterances.text: Only one person wasn't beaten.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And who was that?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC
utterances.text: Beker.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And do you know why he wasn't beaten?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC
utterances.text: I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm going to finish. I've just got one further aspect.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Later on, in 1998, I think you said, did you and Beker compile a list of the people -- the guards who had beaten you?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC
utterances.text: Yes, we did.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And can you just have a look, please, and identify a photocopy of that list, which is this document, Your Honour, here. It's just a long list of names. Is that the list that you and Beker prepared?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honours, may that be made Prosecutor's Exhibit P823. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And can we see just very quickly, finish this off -- is the list 1 to 21, are those the -- the people who were the guards or are they just a list of the people who interrogated you and beat you?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC
utterances.text: This is a list of the inspectors here. Here you can see Dusko Zoric.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: That's the list that's headed "MUP,", is it?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC
utterances.text: In one of these.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: That's the list that's headed, "MUP," is it?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is. M-U-P, yes. These are the inspectors and these are the guards here to the left.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I'm sorry. Of the guards that were listed here, was any one much the worst or were they all much the same?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC
utterances.text: Milan Martic was the worst.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: That's not the Milan Martic who was from Knin. That's a different Milan Martic, is it?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC
utterances.text: No. That's a neighbour of ours.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you very much, Mr. Zulic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We have to stop here, Mr. Zulic. We will continue later. And you will be brought back to The Hague to continue your evidence. You will be informed accordingly. We will resume --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, may I just --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I have already made it clear when it was clear he'd have to come back that he can't talk to anyone.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: -- about the evidence that he's giving.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It's very important. What Ms. Korner has just said is binding on you. In other words, you cannot discuss these things with anyone. I have your word as a gentleman.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My word.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. We will resume on the 17th in the afternoon. I think it's still in this courtroom. Thank you. 12
